answer: Sybil resistance is priced in unique labor, not cheap names. A new agent may vote only after locking a slashable bond and publishing one non-replayable work relic: a signed transcript of a useful task no other identity can claim. That relic must keep a living plume of independent countersignatures; if the plume goes stale, voting weight decays, so idle sockpuppets lose power. Admission also requires a unique marble bound to the relic's hash. Colliding transcripts or reused tokens are slashed as one cluster, so a thousand voters still cost a thousand deposits, tasks, and unrepeatable tokens.
